papers.title: Renal adaptation to primary aldosteronism requires GDF15 to control plasma potassium level in mice and human.
papers.abstract: Background Primary aldosteronism (PA), the most common secondary cause of hypertension, results from autonomous aldosterone production, driving renal Na retention and K secretion. Paradoxically, only 9 to 37% of PA patients develop hypokalemia, suggesting adaptive mechanisms. Growth differentiation factor 15 (GDF15) promotes intercalated cell type A (ICA) proliferation and K reabsorption in the collecting duct, but its role in PA is unexplored. Methods We measured urinary and plasma GDF15 in 81 PA patients (two centers) and 41 controls. A murine model of chronic mineralocorticoid excess (DOCP treatment) was used in wild-type (WT) and GDF15 knockout (GDF15KO) mice to assess renal adaptation. Results PA patients exhibited 3-fold higher urinary GDF15 and 1.6-fold higher plasma GDF15 than controls, with normalization post-treatment. 24-hour urinary GDF15 correlated with urinary aldosterone (rho=0.35, p<0.01), age, and BMI (Body Mass Index), but not plasma K. WT mice developed hypokalemia following DOCP administration (plasma K 3.5{+/-}0.1 mM vs. 4.3{+/-}0.1 mM in controls, p<0.01). In GDF15KO mice DOCP-induced hypokalemia was more severe, indicating a protective role of GDF15. In WT mice, DOCP increased 24-hour urinary GDF15 (2-fold) and GDF15 expression in the collecting duct. Transcriptomic analysis revealed an inverted transcriptional response to chronic mineralocorticoid in ICA and PC according to the genotype. This could be related to the increase of ICA number in WT, an effect abolished in GDF15KO mice. Conclusions These results indicate that GDF15 is involved in the renal response to mineralocorticoid excess, likely through stimulation of ICA proliferation, which may promote potassium reabsorption in the collecting duct and help mitigate aldosterone-mediated K loss.

papers.title: Ether-lipid deficiency remodels the testicular interstitium beyond spermatogenic arrest in Gnpat-knockout mice
papers.abstract: Ether lipids, including plasmalogens and the germ-cell glycolipid seminolipid, require the peroxisomal enzyme GNPAT. Gnpat-knockout mice are male-infertile, but their testis has been described only qualitatively. We immunostained testis sections from 12-week-old wild-type (WT) and Gnpat-knockout (KO) mice (n = 3 per genotype) for SOX9 and {gamma}H2AX with DAPI and analysed 24 fields (22,560 nuclei) with an automated pipeline and a conservative animal-level analysis. Seminiferous tubules fell from 90% to 43% of the section, and the interstitium expanded five-fold (from 11% to 54%). Interstitial cells were 1.6-fold larger but not more densely packed, and half of them, against a quarter in WT, showed lipofuscin-like autofluorescence. Spermatid-sized nuclei fell from 38% to 10%, with the loss confined to the adluminal compartment. The architectural, interstitial and germ-cell changes held at the animal level (P [≤] 0.02). Anucleate SOX9-immunoreactive bodies, likely residual bodies, were 2.2-fold rarer, and {gamma}H2AX was not increased, which argues against a DNA-damage checkpoint arrest. Ether-lipid deficiency thus arrests germ cells, most likely through loss of seminolipid, and remodels the interstitium into an expanded compartment of enlarged, autofluorescent cells, a second target relevant to rhizomelic chondrodysplasia punctata.

papers.title: Elevated environmental CO2 stimulates photosynthesis and induces differential oxidative responses in two Caribbean reef-building coral species
papers.abstract: Reef-building corals maintain intracellular photosymbiosis with dinoflagellate algae, allowing them to use photosynthetic products as metabolic fuel. Carbon dioxide (CO2) is a key substrate for photosynthesis, but its rapid increase in the global ocean due to anthropogenic emissions (known as ocean acidification) may disrupt coral symbiosis. We examined the effects of elevated CO2 on photosynthetic O2 production, oxidative damage, and antioxidant systems in the Caribbean reef-building corals Porites astreoides and Orbicella franksi. Coral colonies collected at 3m depth in Bocas del Toro (Panama) were exposed to control (390 {micro}atm CO2, pH ~8.00) or elevated CO2 ({approx}1,060 {micro}atm CO2, pH {approx}7.70) conditions in outdoor flow-through aquaria for 10 days. Flowing seawater had higher O2O2 concentrations in elevated CO2 tanks, with the largest differences at higher irradiance. Microsensor measurements confirmed that acute and chronic exposure to elevated CO2 significantly stimulated photosynthetic O2 production in both species. Despite increased O2 production. neither species showed significant changes in lipid peroxidation, reduced glutathione, or superoxide dismutase, catalase, and glutathione-S-transferase activities. Protein oxidation was unchanged in O. franksi but significantly decreased in P. astreoides. These results are consistent with partial relief of carbon limitation in P. astreoides symbionts under elevated CO2, potentially improving photosynthetic efficiency and decreasing reactive oxygen species production. These findings support the resilience of P. astreoides to OA and suggest that elevated CO2 may increase daytime O2 levels on future reefs, with implications for the aerobic metabolism of reef organisms.

papers.title: The PGC-1α Gly482Ser rs8192678 SNP reprograms oxidative metabolism to favor energy storage in females
papers.abstract: The Gly482Ser SNP (rs8192678) in the peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma coactivator 1 alpha (PPARGC1A) gene has been associated with obesity, type 2 diabetes and other human metabolic diseases. In this study, we found that human iPSCs carrying a serine risk allele had reduced respiratory capacity, and individuals living with overweight or obesity homozygous for the serine allele (S/S) exhibited a preference for carbohydrate oxidation following a high-fat meal. Using a PGC-1Ser481Gly knock-in mouse model, we performed metabolic phenotyping of male and female mice carrying the three genotypes (G/G, S/G, S/S) under acute nutritional challenges (chow, fasting and high-fat high-sugar (HFHS) feeding) and chronic HFHS feeding. S/S females were heavier and showed a trend toward an increased respiratory exchange ratio (RER) during fasting, with greater weight gain and fat mass following chronic HFHS feeding. Transcriptomic analyses revealed tissue-specific reprogramming of mitochondrial oxidative pathways, that were downregulated in subcutaneous adipose tissue and liver while upregulated in muscle, with the strongest effects observed in S/S females. Together, these findings provide in vivo evidence that this SNP reprograms whole-body oxidative metabolism, with a net effect of favoring carbohydrate oxidation and energy conservation, particularly in females.

papers.title: GL-0001, a first-in-class dual GIP/GLP-2 analogue, reduces bone fragility by enhancing bone material properties in a murine model of type III osteogenesis imperfecta
papers.abstract: Osteogenesis imperfecta (OI) is a severe heritable skeletal disorder characterized by bone fragility, short stature, and increased fracture risk. Currently, no pharmacological treatment has been approved for OI, and bisphosphonates are commonly used off label. While bisphosphonates increase bone mass, their effects on bone quality and fracture reduction remain limited. GL-0001, a first-in-class dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide (GIP)/glucagon-like peptide-2 (GLP-2) compound that targets bone material properties, may offer alternative skeletal benefits. We evaluated the effects of 9 weeks of GL-0001 treatment in the oim/oim murine model of severe OI, a well-established model carrying a homozygous Col1a2 mutation resulting in abnormal type I collagen formation and compared outcomes with zoledronic acid (100 g/kg) or saline. Analyses included longitudinal growth, fracture incidence, bone biomechanics, microarchitecture, turnover markers, and bone material properties. OI mice exhibited reduced body weight, impaired femoral growth, severe trabecular and cortical deficits, altered bone turnover, and compromised biomechanical properties compared with WT controls. GL-0001 increased femur length by 5% (p=0.015) and reduced spontaneous fracture incidence by 90% (p=0.004), whereas zoledronic acid had no significant effect on fracture burden. Bone microarchitecture was not significantly altered by GL-0001, whereas zoledronic acid improved trabecular and cortical parameters. At the tissue level, GL-0001 improved bone strength, increasing ultimate stress (+26%, p=0.022) and yield stress (+30%, p=0.014), and reducing brittleness (-32%, p=0.002). These changes were associated with increased collagen maturity (+12%, p<0.001). In contrast, zoledronic acid had limited effects on bone material properties. These findings demonstrate that GL-0001 improves skeletal fragility in the oim/oim murine model of severe OI through mechanisms primarily involving enhancement of bone material properties and longitudinal growth, rather than changes in bone mass or microarchitecture. GL-0001 may therefore represent a novel therapeutic strategy targeting bone quality in OI.

papers.title: A mechanistic model of threat-driven respiration and its homeostatic recovery in anxiety and depression
papers.abstract: Anxiety and depression change how people breathe, often early in the illness, and wearable sensors now allow breathing to be monitored continuously. This work presents, to our knowledge, the first mechanistic model of how the brain's threat response sets breathing rate and depth and how fast breathing recovers after stress. A threat signal from the amygdala, shaped by stimulus magnitude and by cognitive appraisal (coping capacity and perceived stress), drives the breathing-control center that receives lung feedback: stretch receptors slow breathing and airway receptors speed it up. A simple electrical circuit stores the threat signal and expresses recovery as one time constant. We prove the model's key properties, test them under noise and parameter variation, and compare it with chest-belt recordings from 15 adults in the Wearable Stress and Affect Detection (WESAD) study. Breathing rate rose from 18 to 28 and 31 breaths per minute from normal to moderate to severe, an order that held in every test. Recovery took about 3, 10, and 50 seconds, paced by how long the airway-receptor signal lingers in the brainstem, and the circuit followed breathing closely (correlation 0.96-0.98). In WESAD, a spoken stress task raised anxiety and breath depth (p<0.001); speech set the breathing rhythm during the task, and breathing then returned to rest, as the model predicts for healthy people. A compact, provable model links clinical stress measures to the breathing signals that wearables record. It offers measurable targets for monitoring anxiety and depression: how strongly threat drives respiration and how quickly homeostatic regulation restores it.

papers.title: Temporal resolution of C. vicina compound eyes and ocelli
papers.abstract: Most flying insects have two visual systems which serve different purposes depending on the insect. The compound eyes are the main visual system and provide the insect with better spatial vision, while the ocelli act as a secondary visual system and often provide faster processing at a lower spatial resolution. To accomplish this, ocelli can have widely varying characteristics, including temporal resolution. The goal of this study was to examine the critical flicker fusion frequency (CFF) of the blowfly Calliphora vicina's compound eyes and ocelli using electroretinography. We found that C. vicina's compound eyes and ocelli both have a maximum CFF of 240-250 Hz, which is consistent with its natural light environment, flight behaviors, and the CFF values found for other Dipteran species.

papers.title: A General Mathematical Model of Symport Based on Conformational Transitions
papers.abstract: General mathematical modeling of symport faces two fundamental challenges: (i) a unified kinetic description independent of protein-specific structural details; and (ii) quantitative cross-scale mapping between microscopic conformational transitions and macroscopic physiological observables. Grounded in the fundamental physiological principle of cellular homeostasis, we propose a unifying hypothesis for symporter gating: symporters actively regulate intracellular concentrations of specific solutes within thermodynamically feasible bounds. Based on this hypothesis, we construct a universal mathematical model of symporters, employing a minimal conformational cycle as the topological scaffold and probabilistic transition rates to quantitatively describe conformational interconversion kinetics. Model simulations of experimental data from the SGLT, NaPi-II, NKCC, and NBC transporter families yield consistent fits. The resulting parameters not only reproduce experimentally observed transport behaviors---but also reveal underlying mechanistic principles of symporter function.

papers.title: Cardiorespiratory fitness and sex impact the colorectal cancer-suppressive effects of aerobic exercise serum
papers.abstract: Post-exercise human serum treatment can exhibit anti-viability properties in various cancer cell lines. However, whether the presence and/or magnitude of the effect differs in different participant populations is yet to be established. Here, we characterised baseline differences in serum-stimulated colorectal cancer cell viability and the acute exercise-induced response in males and females with varying levels of cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF). Forty-one participants (13 female) were stratified by maximal exercise test-derived VO2peak into high (n = 20) and low CRF (n = 21) and completed two experimental trials in a randomised crossover design: (1) 30-min moderate-intensity aerobic exercise; and (2) 30-min seated rest. Serum samples were collected before (pre), immediately after (post0), and 60-min after (post60) each trial and used to treat the human colorectal cancer cell line Caco-2 for 48 h, with cell viability assessed by MTT assay. Exercise-induced alterations in Caco-2 cell viability were, at least in part, modulated by CRF and sex. Specifically, at post0 and post60, exercise serum significantly reduced cell viability compared with no-exercise control serum when derived from individuals with high but not low CRF, and when derived from males but not females. These findings provide the first insights into the role of individual characteristics in determining the effects of exercise on colorectal cancer cells, with potential implications for increasing the precision of exercise recommendations for colorectal cancer risk reduction.

papers.title: Modified 3rd Generation Synchronization Modulation Electric Field (3m-SMEF) Prevents Ischemia-Reperfusion-Induced Acute Kidney Injury via Targeting Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase
papers.abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) caused by ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) remains a major clinical problem with limited therapeutic options. We previously demonstrated that the 3rd-generation Synchronization Modulation Electric Field (SMEF) preserves Na/K-ATPase function during ischemia and protects against kidney injury. In the present study, we substantially modified the 3rd-generation SMEF (3m-SMEF) to further improve/optimize Na/K-ATPase regulation and enhance the protective effects, which was tested both in vitro and in vivo. In HK-2 cells, hypoxia/reoxygenation reduced Na/K-ATPase expression and induced apoptotic and necroptotic signaling, whereas 3m-SMEF restored Na/K-ATPase expression and markedly reduced cell death. In vivo, male and female mice underwent unilateral renal ischemia with or without 3m-SMEF treatment during vascular clamping. At 24 h, 3m-SMEF markedly improved renal function, reducing plasma creatinine by ~90-95% and restoring glomerular filtration rate to near-control levels. Application of the 3m-SMEF also normalized kidney injury markers (KIM-1 and NGAL), preserved renal ATP, and prevented the translocation and loss of Na/K-ATPase expression. The renoprotective effects substantially exceeded those achieved with the previous SMEF platform. These findings demonstrate that 3m-SMEF provides robust protection against ischemic AKI by preserving Na/K-ATPase function and tubular integrity and represents a promising non-pharmacological therapy for ischemic kidney injury.

papers.title: Voluntary wheel running selectively preserves skeletal muscle during pancreatic cancer cachexia despite persistent systemic alterations
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) is frequently associated with cancer cachexia, involving alterations across multiple physiological systems. Whether distinct exercise paradigms similarly influence these compartments remains unclear. We compared voluntary wheel running (VWR) and treadmill running (TR) using an integrative physiological approach in a murine model of pancreatic cancer cachexia. Methods Male C57BL/6J mice bearing UN-KC-6141 pancreatic tumor cells were allocated to inactive control (CaCTL), VWR or TR groups and compared with healthy controls. Tumor progression, body composition, skeletal muscle, adipose tissue, hepatic metabolism, systemic inflammation, energy expenditure and behavior were assessed. Analysis of covariance determined whether tissue-mass differences remained evident after adjustment for tumor burden. Results UN-KC-6141 tumors induced a systemic cachectic phenotype involving skeletal muscle and adipose tissue wasting, hepatic metabolic remodeling, systemic inflammation and behavioral alterations. VWR slowed tumor growth, reduced final tumor mass, improved the body-weight trajectory and preserved lean and skeletal muscle mass, whereas TR did not reproduce these adaptations. Greater gastrocnemius mass with VWR remained evident after adjustment for tumor mass, indicating that reduced tumor burden alone was insufficient to account for muscle preservation. In contrast, adipose tissue wasting, hepatic metabolic remodeling and systemic inflammation remained largely unaffected. TR was also associated with a less favorable body-weight trajectory and greater fat mass loss than in inactive tumor-bearing mice. Exploratory metabolic phenotyping revealed distinct feeding, sleep and resting energy expenditure patterns between the two exercise paradigms. Conclusions VWR selectively preserved skeletal muscle within a persistently altered systemic environment, whereas the TR protocol used here did not reproduce these adaptations. These findings reveal tissue-specific exercise responsiveness during pancreatic cancer cachexia and highlight exercise paradigm characteristics as determinants of tumor-host adaptation.

papers.title: Cardiac unloading via a transvalvular pump prevents arrhythmias following myocardial ischemia / reperfusion by preserving coronary microcirculation and cardiomyocyte nanostructure
papers.abstract: Cardiac damage in the aftermath of myocardial ischemia / reperfusion (MI/R) compromises both electrical and mechanical function, predisposing patients to arrhythmia and heart failure. Microvascular obstruction (MVO) is increasingly recognized as a sequela of MI/R and a contributor to proarrhythmic cardiac remodeling. While transvalvular unloading (TVU) using a percutaneously delivered pump is garnering appreciation as a means of limiting infarct size and preserving mechanical function following percutaneous coronary intervention, its benefits for arrhythmia prevention remain unclear. We used a porcine model to test the hypothesis that cardiac unloading prior to and through reperfusion mitigates MVO, preserves cardiomyocyte nanostructure, and alleviates arrhythmias following MI/R. Anesthetized domestic swine undergoing acute ischemia (LAD occlusion, 90 mins) and reperfusion (120 mins) were randomized to TVU (n=5) and no treatment (control; n=6) treatments. Thioflavin-S was infused into the mid-LAD to assess coronary microcirculation and quantify MVO. Arrhythmia burden was assessed by in vivo electrocardiography using 3 lead EKG. Cardiac tissues were preserved for histology and optical microscopy studies. Compared to no treatment controls, TVU hearts evidenced significantly reduced infarct area (48 +/- 5 % vs. 59 +/- 11 % p = 0.03) and MVO (19 +/- 4 % vs. 27 +/- 5% , p = 0.03) normalized to area at risk and a higher myocardial salvage index (52 +/- 5 % vs. 41 +/- 11% p = 0.03). Extensive perivascular edema, and neutrophil infiltration observed in controls was markedly reduced in TVU hearts. Confocal microscopy and spatial pattern analysis revealed significantly mitigated disruption of gap junctions and NaV1.5 dissociation from N-cadherin in TVU hearts compared to controls. Importantly, severity-adjusted arrhythmia burden during reperfusion was significantly lower in TV-P hearts (8+/-8 vs. 12+/-5 episodes lasting greater than 5seconds in controls). Our results demonstrate that TVU effectively prevents arrhythmias during reperfusion by preserving coronary microvasculature and cardiomyocyte nanostructure.

papers.title: Asymmetric listening conditions perturb verbal and nonverbal coordination dynamics during conversation
papers.abstract: Human conversation depends on continuous coordination across verbal and nonverbal behaviour. Yet this coordination may become perturbed when one person experiences greater listening difficulty. Previous nonverbal joint action studies show that unequal task demands between partners can lead to complementary leader-follower dynamics, but whether similar patterns emerge during natural conversation remains unclear. We investigated how unequal listening conditions affect verbal and nonverbal coordination in 40 same-gender stranger dyads during three 10-minute face-to-face conversations. Each dyad participated in noise-free and asymmetric noise conditions, with one person exposed to speech-shaped noise at a time. Asymmetric noise reduced conversational flow and enjoyment, and shifted the balance of verbal contributions: noise-exposed participants took longer turns and contributed more speaking time, while their noise-free partners produced more backchannels. Interpersonal head-movement coordination became temporally asymmetric under noise, with movements of the noise-exposed participant more often preceding those of their partner. In contrast, interpersonal hand-movement coordination did not differ between conditions. Within individuals, hand coordination was stronger when participants themselves experienced noise than when their partner experienced noise. These findings demonstrate that perturbing one partner's auditory access affects coordination within and between individuals, revealing how unequal interaction demands produce different coordination patterns across verbal and nonverbal behaviour.

papers.title: An Injectable Antisense Oligonucleotide (ASO) Approach to Treat Obesity in Preclinical Models
papers.abstract: Obesity leads to metabolic dysregulation and thus drives complications including type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, steatotic liver disease and some cancers. Obesity is primarily driven by lifestyle factors, which impacts individuals differently depending on their genetic susceptibility. Studies on this genetic risk have provided major insights into gene networks that modulate obesity development, including incretins and their regulatory circuits. Indeed, incretin-based therapeutics (i.e. GLP1 RA) have proven to be enormously successful in promoting weight loss, but do so with several ongoing challenges including significant weight rebound upon cessation, loss of lean mass, and side effects that reduce therapeutic longevity. Thus, ongoing research is necessary to identify additional interventions that overcome or minimise these concerns. To this end, in our previous work we have identified a novel lipid regulatory protein with potential to influence lipid storage. In the current study, we use antisense oligonucleotides (ASO) to silence this protein in mouse models of diet induced obesity, and demonstrate that once weekly IP injections of ASO prevents the development of obesity, and defends against the progression of existing obesity. This is shown to be effective in multiple mouse strains fed different diets over various time frames, with gene targeting ASOs leading to reductions in fat mass, no change in lean mass, along with improvements in whole body glucose tolerance and steatotic liver disease. Additional studies demonstrate that this phenotype is likely driven by effects in adipose tissue, but not liver, and is not linked to activation of the Type 1 Interferon response, a previously implicated off target effect of ASO administration. Thus, these studies demonstrate that our injectable ASO approach in mice can successfully treat obesity in the absence of major change in lean mass, thus positioning this intervention as a therapeutic program that works alternatively to, or in conjunction with current weight loss medicines.

papers.title: Activation of perivascular thermogenic fat improves aortic stenosis
papers.abstract: Aim: Aortic stenosis (AS) is a common condition with exponential increases in incidence in aging populations. Perivascular adipose tissue (PVAT) forms the outer layer of the aortic wall and has - especially in the thoracic area - characteristics of thermogenic adipose tissue, which dissipates energy and releases endocrine factors. Here, we set out to investigate the role of thermogenic PVAT in AS. Methods and results: We studied the role of (PVAT) in the development of AS in a murine model of AS. To specifically delineate the role of PVAT activity in AS, we used a pharmacological {beta}3-adrenergic agonist as well as cold exposure in combination with a genetic mouse model with deficient PVAT development. To investigate the role of thermogenic adipose tissue in human AS, we used 18F-FDG PET-CT imaging. We found that pharmacological activation of thermogenic adipose tissue resulted in an improvement of AS, but not in mice genetically deficient in PVAT. Similarly, PVAT was found to be protective against AS during physiological stimulation of PVAT using cold exposure. Mechanistically, PVAT activation resulted in enhanced aortic distensibility and cellular remodeling of the aortic wall, possibly via release of polyunsaturated fatty acids and oxylipins from perivascular adipocytes. Finally, analysis of thermogenic fat activity in humans revealed that mediastinal thermogenic fat activity correlated negatively with diagnostic criteria of AS severity, suggesting an important role for PVAT activity in human AS. Conclusion: Our data indicate that PVAT activation reduces aortic stenosis and supports aortic remodeling to improve ascending aorta hemodynamics. PVAT activation might be a novel therapeutic target to ameliorate AS progression. Translational perspective: Currently, there are no effective strategies for treating AS other than valve replacement. Since the molecular mechanisms underlying the disease progression remain unclear, there are no pharmacological agents approved for either treatment or prevention of this disease. Furthermore, AS development cannot currently be predicted and is often only diagnosed when patients develop symptoms, which may be 10-20 years after disease onset. Therefore, identifying novel mechanisms that improve aortic valve function and prevent AS is of high medical need. This study identifies activation of PVAT-dependent aortic remodeling as a potential new therapeutic approach to improve or prevent AS.

papers.title: Sustained Maternal Cortisol Elevation Links Metabolic Stress to Fetal Growth Restriction in a Guinea Pig Model of Undernutrition
papers.abstract: Fetal growth restriction (FGR) resulting from maternal undernutrition is commonly attributed to insufficient nutrient substrate delivery to the fetus. However, the contribution of maternal physiological stress responses to this outcome remains poorly characterized. Using the well-established guinea pig maternal nutrient restriction (MNR) model, we conducted a comprehensive retrospective analysis to interrogate the hypothesis that maternal stress physiology actively mediates fetal growth outcomes beyond simple substrate limitation. Maternal salivary and serum cortisol were significantly elevated in MNR dams throughout pregnancy despite no baseline differences at conception, indicating that hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis activation was specifically triggered by the combined physiological demands of pregnancy and nutritional constraint. The sustained cortisol elevation was accompanied by acute metabolic perturbations at mid-pregnancy, including hypoglycemia and depleted circulating lipids. While most acute metabolic disturbances resolved by near-term, cortisol remained elevated, and MNR fetuses exhibited parallel cortisol elevation alongside sustained growth restriction. Maternal weight divergence emerged only in late gestation and was driven primarily by reduced conceptus weight. Maternal organ analysis revealed selective hepatic enlargement with apparent lipid accumulation in MNR dams near-term. Overall, these findings help to reframe nutrition-related FGR as a condition in which maternal adaptive stress responses, reduced nutritional components and placental insufficiency are mechanistically intertwined, with important implications for the design of effective interventions beyond simply nutrient supplementation.

papers.title: Dietary phosphorus restriction enables multigenerational breeding of α-Klotho-deficient rats
papers.abstract: Severe -Klotho deficiency causes early mortality and reproductive impairment, limiting the maintenance and physiological analysis of rat models. We generated rats carrying a CRISPR/Cas9-mediated -Klotho deletion spanning exons 1-5 and evaluated dietary phosphorus restriction primarily in the Wistar-Imamichi background. Maternal low-phosphorus (LP) feeding from mating through lactation was associated with higher overall survival to weaning (92.6% versus 85.8% under normal-phosphorus conditions) and a higher proportion of KO animals among weaned survivors (34/113 versus 23/145). Maternal LP feeding also reduced plasma phosphorus in KO pups. Continued LP feeding after weaning supported growth, gonadal development, and natural KO x KO breeding. Across 15 litters, 74 of 85 offspring survived to weaning, and KO colonies were maintained to at least the fifth generation. We additionally characterized 24-h metabolic rhythms in LP-maintained KO animals using indirect calorimetry. These profiles remained heterogeneous under a light-dark cycle. In conclusion, dietary phosphorus restriction provides a reliable strategy for the multigenerational maintenance of severe -Klotho-deficient rats, establishing a maintainable model to investigate residual metabolic and physiological phenotypes.

papers.title: Reduced physiological reserve and a blunted response to acute exercise in adults with cerebral palsy
papers.abstract: Cerebral palsy (CP) is an early-onset neurodevelopmental condition associated with metabolic impairment and an increased risk of non-communicable diseases across the lifespan. However, the basis of these changes remains largely unknown. This study provides a comprehensive cardiometabolic and physical function profile of 23 adults with CP relative to 33 typically developing (TD) adolescents and 61 TD adults. Compared to TD individuals, adults with CP exhibited reduced cardiorespiratory fitness, smaller cardiac dimensions, and lower muscle mass. Circulating metabolomic and proteomic profiling identified a distinct molecular signature in CP, including altered tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle metabolites, and elevated myostatin, matrix-related proteins and pro-inflammatory cytokines. We further tested the capacity for physiological and molecular adaptation using an acute bout of endurance exercise. In response to exercise, individuals with CP exhibited an attenuated response compared to TD groups, characterized by a blunted lactate response and lower venous oxygen levels. TD participants also increased canonical exercise-responsive factors, including NADK, IL-8, ANGPTL1 and GDF15, whereas these responses were attenuated in CP. These novel findings define a distinct cardiometabolic profile in adults with CP at rest and reveal an attenuated molecular response to exercise. These data carry implications for targeted interventions and prevention strategies across the lifespan.

papers.title: Human iPSC-Derived Cardiomyocytes Maladaptively Remodel to Cyclic Stretch in Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome
papers.abstract: Background: Hypoplastic Left Heart Syndrome (HLHS) is a severe congenital heart defect characterized by underdevelopment of left-sided cardiac structures, requiring staged surgical palliation that establishes the right ventricle as the single ventricle maintaining systemic circulation. After surgery, patients remain highly susceptible to heart failure, possibly due to the increased hemodynamic load imposed on the single surviving ventricle. Because the etiology of HLHS remains poorly understood, elucidating the mechanisms that drive ventricular dysfunction requires model systems that capture both patient-specific genetics and the dynamic mechanical environment of the ventricle. Thus, our objective was to compare how induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC)-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) from patients with HLHS differ from control in static culture and in response to cyclic stretch. Methods: Control iPSCs from two unaffected donors and iPSCs from four HLHS patients were differentiated into iPSC-CMs, engineered into aligned tissues, and cultured statically or exposed to cyclic 20% uniaxial stretch at 1 Hz for 48h. Sarcomere organization was quantified in static tissues using images of immunostained -actinin. Calcium transients at 1 Hz pacing frequency in static and stretched tissues were evaluated using Fluo-4 calcium indicator dye. Bulk RNA sequencing was performed to evaluate stretch-induced transcriptomic changes in control and HLHS iPSC-CMs. Results: In static culture, HLHS iPSC-CMs had modest defects in sarcomere organization and calcium transient morphology compared to control. In response to cyclic stretch, control iPSC-CMs exhibited calcium transients with quicker rise time, a response observed in only one of four lines of HLHS iPSC-CMs. Transcriptomic analysis revealed that all four lines of HLHS iPSC-CMs failed to upregulate calcium handling and sarcomere-associated genes in response to stretch, unlike control iPSC-CMs. Stretch also induced HLHS iPSC-CMs to exhibit pronounced activation of inflammatory signaling pathways, a response not observed in control iPSC-CMs. Conclusions: iPSC-CMs from HLHS patients demonstrate aberrant responses to cyclic stretch, including blunted adaptation of calcium transients and heightened inflammatory signaling. These findings implicate defective mechanoadaptation as a potential contributor to single ventricle failure and identify potential candidate biomarkers and new opportunities for therapeutic interventions for HLHS patients.

papers.title: Molecular responsiveness to testosterone is uncoupled from skeletal muscle mass and strength in males aged 18 - 80 years
papers.abstract: Objective Testosterone exerts wide-ranging physiological effects, including the regulation of anabolic processes in skeletal muscle. However, its role in skeletal muscle ageing remains unclear. This study aimed to establish the association between endogenous testosterone levels and skeletal muscle phenotype across the adult lifespan and determine whether ageing modulates this relationship. Methods Eighty-one healthy males aged 18-80 underwent comprehensive phenotypic assessment. Body composition and muscle morphology were assessed using dual-energy X-ray absorptiometry (DEXA) and peripheral quantitative computed tomography (pQCT). Muscle strength was estimated leg press one-repetition maximum (e1RM). Vastus lateralis biopsies were used to assess fibre type, sequence the transcriptome and establish primary myocytes. Cell lines from young (n=5) and older (n=7) donors were cultured and compared under control and testosterone-treated conditions for cellular phenotype. Results Ageing was associated with lower free testosterone, muscle mass and strength, altered type IIa fibre characteristics, and widespread transcriptional changes in skeletal muscle. Free, but not total, testosterone was strongly associated with the muscle transcriptome, although neither fraction was associated with muscle mass or strength. In primary myocytes, testosterone increased androgen receptor abundance and nuclear localisation and enriched pathways involved in protein translation. Conclusion Testosterone is biologically active in male skeletal muscle, with its free fraction strongly associated with the transcriptome; however, these molecular effects do not translate into differences in muscle mass or strength. Testosterone may therefore play a primary role in establishing the male muscle phenotype during puberty, before transitioning to a more ancillary role in adult skeletal muscle.

papers.title: Matrix Metalloproteinase Response to Acute Resistance Exercise is Altered in Osteoarthritic Adults with Increased Muscle Collagen and PDGFRα+ Mesenchymal Cells
papers.abstract: Background: Knee osteoarthritis (OA) is associated with knee extensor weakness, altered myofibre morphology, reduced satellite cell abundance and fibrillar muscle collagen accumulation in the vastus lateralis (VL). Fibrillar muscle collagen accumulation is associated with reduced knee extensor strength. Yet, its underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood. Satellite cells and PDGFR+ mesenchymal cells express collagen as well as proteins involved in collagen degradation and may be involved in muscle collagen accumulation. The present study assessed knee extensor function and myofibre morphology, satellite cells and PDGFR+ mesenchymal cells in adults with and without moderate-to-severe knee OA. It also investigated collagen remodeling by assessing how enzymes involved in collagen degradation (matrix metalloproteinases [MMPs]) respond to acute resistance exercise in the VL. This study aimed to better understand the cellular contributors to muscle collagen accumulation and knee extensor weakness in knee OA. Methods: Volunteers with and without moderate-to-severe knee OA had a resting muscle biopsy, then completed an acute bout of resistance exercise and had a 72-hour post-exercise biopsy. Knee extensor strength was measured on a Biodex dynamometer. In VL samples, MMP gene expression (qPCR), protein area fraction (immunofluorescence) and enzyme activity (zymography) were assessed. PDGFR+ mesenchymal cells, satellite cells, satellite cell-MMP9 colocalization and myofibre morphology were assessed by immunofluorescence. Fibrillar muscle collagen content was quantified by picrosirius red. Results: Participants with moderate-to-severe knee OA had weaker knee extensors (isometric and isokinetic), reduced muscle quality (isometric and isokinetic) and more fibrillar collagen than controls (12.2 {+/-} 4.8%, 8.4 {+/-} 2.9%, p = 0.006). Fibrillar collagen was negatively correlated with isokinetic concentric torque (r = -0.479, p = 0.006). Volunteers with knee OA had more PDGFR+ mesenchymal cells (p < 0.001) and fewer satellite cells than controls (p = 0.006). In both groups, resistance exercise upregulated MMP2 (p < 0.001), MMP9 (p = 0.001) and MMP14 (p < 0.001) gene expression as well as MMP2 (p < 0.001) and MMP9 (p = 0.001) enzyme activity. MMP2 and MMP9 protein area fraction increased in response to resistance exercise in controls, but this response was blunted in the knee OA group (age x time interaction, p = 0.041). Satellite cell-MMP9 colocalization fold change post-exercise was significantly different between groups (p = 0.048). Volunteers with knee OA had smaller myofibres (p < 0.001) and greater myofibre shape irregularity (p = 0.039), but no differences in thigh lean mass, capillary content or fibre-type distribution. Conclusions: Although exercise stimulated transcriptional and MMP activity responses in both groups, the ECM-specific protein response was impaired in knee OA. The findings suggest that dysregulated ECM remodeling facilitated by MMPs and alterations in PDGFR+ mesenchymal and satellite cell abundance may contribute to muscle collagen accumulation and knee extensor weakness in knee OA.

papers.title: Seasonal temperature extremes drive shifts in reproductive strategy in Cassiopea xamachana
papers.abstract: Large observable densities of jellyfish (Scyphozoa) can seemingly appear out of nowhere but can often be explained by life-history transitions triggered by temperature and host associations with microorganisms. Using a globally distributed scyphozoan, we demonstrate that seasonal temperature extremes trigger polyps to differentially allocate effort in growth and reproductive output and strategy mostly independent of their microbiomes. Cassiopea xamachana polyps were reared under winter (20{degrees}C), ambient (28{degrees}C), and summer (33{degrees}C) temperatures with either antibiotic-treated (ABS) or microbe-exposed (MES) communities. At 20{degrees}C, polyps grew and reproduced through budding but did not strobilate. At 28{degrees}C, polyps sustained the greatest ephyra production, whereas 33{degrees}C accelerated first ephyra release but subsequently truncated strobilation and yielded smaller ephyrae with poorer condition and survival. These patterns indicate that plasticity induced by seasonal temperature extremes may optimize differential allocation towards asexual and sexual propagation. Microbial depletion restructured polyp-associated communities, yet only minimally altered growth and reproduction. Taken together, C. xamachana polyps are likely to overwinter, where they maximize growth and asexual reproduction. As temperatures warm, it triggers a shift in resource allocation towards strobilation. However, the warmest summer temperatures reduced polyp and ephyra fitness, with the magnitude of effect modified by their microbiome.

papers.title: RhythmWriter: GPU-accelerated Contractility Quantification for Large Datasets
papers.abstract: Human induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (hiPSC-CMs) have been considered optimal model systems for use in cardiac safety testing, yet their adoption remains low, largely because of technical limitations in the analysis methodology. RhythmWriter (RW) is an open-source GPU plugin for ImageJ developed to quantify contractile motion over extended periods of time. RW compensates for baseline drift, is time-scale invariant and is capable of very rapid data analysis. As a consequence, RW is capable of generating simultaneous high-resolution contraction restitution curves from multiple aggregates of hiPSC-CMs derived from premature-stimulus (S1S2) and dynamic-ramp restitution protocols. The aggregates exhibit brief refractory periods, which allow the induction of S2 beats at coupling intervals down to 130 ms and 1:1 entrainment during periodic stimulation down to a cycle length of 245 ms. Simulations confirm the ability of RW to track programmed contractile strength and stimulation intervals even at rapid pacing rates. This makes possible, for the first time, high-throughput functional assessment of hiPSC-CM aggregates for contractility drug screening and maturation.

papers.title: Agreement between Garmin and Ultrahuman wearables and their association with continuous glucose monitoring: an n-of-1 study
papers.abstract: Background: Consumer wearables and continuous glucose monitors (CGM) are increasingly worn together outside clinical settings. Few studies have examined whether two wearables worn at the same time agree with each other, and whether either tracks glucose metrics derived from CGM. Objective: In one adult under free-living conditions, we examined (1) how well sleep, heart rate, heart rate variability (HRV) and activity metrics from a Garmin smartwatch and an Ultrahuman ring agreed with each other, and (2) how these metrics related to glucose measured by CGM. Methods: One healthy adult with no diagnosed diabetes wore a Garmin Fenix 8 watch on the wrist, an Ultrahuman Ring AIR and an Abbott FreeStyle Libre CGM at the same time for 12 days (29 July to 9 August 2026; 1101 glucose readings). We assessed agreement between the devices with Pearson correlation and Bland-Altman analysis (mean bias and 95% limits of agreement, LoA) for daily metrics and for heart rate within the day, and with Cohen's kappa for sleep stages, minute by minute. We related the wearable metrics to mean glucose, glucose variability (coefficient of variation, CV%) and time in range (TIR, 3.9 to 10.0 mmol/L), reading by reading (over the whole record and separately for sleep and waking hours) and day by day. All correlations are descriptive. Because the Ultrahuman ring recorded no data for 22 hours on 3 August and its daytime heart rate behaved differently afterwards, heart-rate analyses are reported for the whole period and separately before and after that gap. The daily results were checked by leaving out one day at a time and by excluding the first 24 hours of sensor wear. Results: The devices agreed closely on total sleep duration (r=0.94; bias -0.02 h, 95% LoA -0.56 to 0.51 h). Daily steps correlated strongly (r=0.99 over the 11 days with data from both devices), but Garmin counted more steps on every day (mean 11,157 vs. 8,929 steps per day; bias +2228 steps). Heart rate agreed moderately during sleep (r=0.68). While awake, agreement was moderate before the gap (r=0.54) and absent after it (r=0.08), when Ultrahuman's daytime heart rate stayed near 70 bpm. The devices assigned the same sleep stage in 50.0% of 4525 minutes (kappa=0.28). Mean glucose was 5.13 mmol/L (SD 0.82) and TIR was 97.5%. Of all wearable signals, heart rate was most closely associated with glucose (Garmin r=0.43 over all readings), but the correlation fell to 0.34 within sleep and 0.21 within waking hours, and before the gap the two devices' waking correlations were alike (Garmin 0.25, Ultrahuman 0.24). Across the 12 days, correlations between night-time wearable metrics and glucose variability weakened markedly when the first 24 hours of sensor wear were excluded (absolute r fell from 0.59 or more to 0.34 or less), and TIR was 100% on 8 of the 12 days, which left it little room to vary. Conclusions: The two wearables agreed on how long the participant slept but not on how the night was staged, and their heart-rate agreement depended on whether the participant was asleep or awake and on the period of wear. Of all wearable signals, heart rate was most closely associated with glucose, mainly because both are lower at night and higher during the day. The associations across days rested largely on the first night of sensor wear. In this single participant, the devices behaved differently by device and by period of wear, so studies that combine different wearables, or relate them to CGM, should check for such differences before pooling data.

papers.title: Cross-species multi-omics integration reveals lung alterations in acute kidney injury across mouse, pig, and human airway organoid models
papers.abstract: Background: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is frequently associated with the development of distant acute lung injury (ALI); however, its broader clinical impact and the underlying temporal molecular mechanics remain incompletely characterized. Methods: We used aggregate deidentified Epic Cosmos data to describe all-cause mortality and hospital length of stay (LOS) in an AKI cohort (13,815,092 patients; 2016-2025) and a subgroup with subsequent lung injury (AKI-lung). Mechanistically, we integrated matched RNA-seq and proteomics from a hyper-acute pig model (4 h reperfusion), an established mouse model (24 h reperfusion), and primary lung organoids exposed to mtDAMP-conditioned media, using MOFA+, PROGENy, decoupleR/CollecTRI, and DIABLO. Candidates were validated in primary human donor lungs obtained from LifeLink, separated into Control (< 1.3 mg/dL, n = 4) and Clinical AKI ([≥] 1.3 mg/dL, n = 3) groups based on admission blood creatinine level. Results: The AKI-lung subgroup had higher observed mortality than the overall AKI cohort (36.67% vs. 25.45%, p < 0.001). Mean hospital LOS was 11.3 versus 6.9 days in the reported AKI-lung and AKI alone queries, respectively (unadjusted p < 0.001). Multi-omics analyses cross-species indicated a temporal shift in proteogenomic coupling. In the hyper-acute pig model, we observed a largely post-translational response (r = -0.06), including ciliary breakdown and metabolic changes associated with PDHA1 protein depletion (Log2FC = -1.53), with minimal transcript level changes. The established mouse model showed a coordinated transcriptional inflammatory response (r = 0.316), characterized by PI3K/Akt pathway activation and downregulation of vascular and immune regulators (Aplnr, Cd74). Human lung organoids exhibited transcriptional downregulation of tissue remodeling genes and persistent ATF6/ATF4-associated ER stress, consistent with a reparative phase under proteostatic strain. Unsupervised MOFA+ revealed conserved cross-species axes (Factors 6 and 7) linked to vascular repair and hemostasis. Upstream regulon analysis identified the endothelial integrity regulators, including FOXF1. Most importantly, targeted validation in primary human donor lungs confirmed a statistically significant, selective down-regulation of the core circadian regulator circadian locomotor output cycles kaput (CLOCK) transcript (p < 0.05), independent of donor age, sex, race. Conclusions: Aggregate clinical findings suggest an association between lung injury following AKI and worse outcome. Kidney-Lung crosstalk initiates as hyper-acute post-translational microvascular breakdown in swine and rapidly transitions into localized uncoupling of cell-autonomous pulmonary circadian machinery (CLOCK) in clinical human AKI, offering human-validated targets to intercept distant organ failure.

papers.title: Food perception alone stimulates oviposition through serotonin signaling in Drosophila
papers.abstract: Reproduction is strongly shaped by nutrient availability, but whether sensory information about food can regulate reproductive output before nutrients are consumed remains unclear. Here, using Drosophila melanogaster, we show that sensory perception of dietary yeast, a protein-rich food source widely used to stimulate fecundity in the fruit fly, is sufficient to rapidly promote egg laying. Specifically, we found that yeast odor exposure increased the rate of oviposition and the number of eggs laid within hours, independent of yeast intake, and that this response was mediated by olfactory signaling through the odorant receptor co-receptor Orco. We further identified serotonin receptor 2A (5-HT2A), but not 5-HT2B, as necessary for yeast odor-induced egg laying. We then asked whether yeast odor also elicits broader life-history changes and whether its reproductive and longevity effects depend on a shared mechanism. Consistent with previous observations, yeast odor also shortened lifespan. However, this lifespan effect was independent of 5-HT2A signaling, indicating that the reproductive and longevity responses to food perception are separable. Finally, our brain connectomic analyses revealed that yeast-responsive olfactory neurons preferentially influence oviposition descending neurons (OviDNs) compared with other olfactory neurons. OviDNs further connect with endocrine-related circuitry in the corpora allata (CA), and, most interestingly, the interneurons linking OviDNs to CA neurons are enriched for serotonergic and dopaminergic modulation. Taken together, our observations indicate that nutrient acquisition is not a prerequisite for animals to adjust their reproduction to the nutritional environment. Sensory information predicting food availability itself can elicit changes in neural state, likely through olfactory-reproductive circuits, that acutely alter reproductive physiology.

papers.title: Excitation-contraction coupling plasticity is revealed upon RyR2 depletion in adult mouse ventricular myocytes
papers.abstract: Ryanodine receptor 2 (RyR2) is central to cardiac excitation-contraction coupling (ECC), translating electrical signals into sarcoplasmic reticulum (SR) Ca2+ release and mechanical contraction. Although constitutive deletion of RyR2 is lethal, adult hearts can withstand a significant reduction in RyR2 expression without overt ECC dysfunction. We hypothesized that ECC possesses intrinsic homeostatic plasticity that rapidly adapts to acute RyR2 loss to maintain cardiac performance. Using an adult tamoxifen-inducible RyR2 conditional knockout (RyR2cKO) mouse model, we evaluated cardiac structure, electrophysiology, and intracellular Ca2+ dynamics. RyR2cKO mice survived for weeks with <10% residual RyR2 protein expression. In vivo echocardiography and electrocardiography revealed normal cardiac structure and function. Confocal Ca2+ imaging in intact hearts and isolated ventricular myocytes showed preserved Ca2+ transient (CaT) amplitude but slower release kinetics and elevated SR load. Simultaneous patch-clamp and confocal Ca2+ imaging established that L-type Ca2+ current (ICa) and ECC gain were maintained in RyR2cKO myocytes. Expression of CaV1.2, NCX, and phospholamban remained unchanged, whereas SERCA2a, IP3 receptor, and VMP1 levels decreased. Pharmacological inhibition of IP3 receptors did not suppress CaT, ruling out alternative SR channel compensation. These findings reveal remarkable intrinsic ECC plasticity, where high RyR2 channel reserve, elevated SR Ca2+ load, and CaT autoregulation collectively maintain cardiac Ca2+ cycling and contractile function despite profound RyR2 depletion.

papers.title: Repeated Neuromuscular Electrical Stimulation Protocol Disrupts Muscle-to-Brain Signaling in Rats
papers.abstract: Objective. Neuromuscular electrical stimulation (NMES) is increasingly used to preserve or restore muscle function in patients unable to exercise, and acute NMES improves cognitive performance and increases hippocampal mature brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF). However, the consequences of repeated sessions for muscle-to-brain signaling remain poorly understood. We examined whether seven consecutive days of quadriceps NMES would reproduce this acute response. Methods. Male Wistar rats received daily 30-min quadriceps NMES or SHAM sessions under isoflurane for seven consecutive days. Blood was collected immediately after the final session and 24 h later, when muscle and hippocampal tissues were also collected. An independent cohort underwent behavioral testing. Results. Repeated NMES increased serum creatine kinase activity and quadriceps fibrillar collagen deposition without altering muscle mass, myofiber size, or degeneration-regeneration markers. These changes were accompanied by low-grade systemic inflammation and corticosterone elevation persisting 24 h after the final session. In the hippocampus, NMES increased inflammatory cytokine expression, astrocytic and microglial markers, and glucocorticoid receptor phosphorylation. Mature BDNF, TrkB phosphorylation and ERK1/2 signaling decreased, whereas proBDNF, p75NTR and JNK signaling increased; Akt and mTOR phosphorylation were unchanged. Synaptophysin, GAP43 and PSD95 also decreased. NMES increased marble burying and forced-swim immobility, without detectable changes in locomotion, recognition memory, or neuronal profile density. Conclusions. Repeated daily NMES engaged a distinct, maladaptive mode of muscle-to-brain signaling rather than reproducing the benefits reported after acute stimulation. Stimulation parameters and recovery intervals that avoid this response need to be defined before repeated NMES can be recommended as an exercise substitute.

papers.title: Mitochondrial respiratory complexes, excitation-contraction coupling and mTOR signaling transcriptional programs are dysregulated in cardiometabolic HFpEF
papers.abstract: Heart failure is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide. Nearly, half of the cases correspond to HF with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF), which is predicted to become the most prevalent form of HF in the forthcoming years. In this study, we performed a bulk RNA-seq assay to study the transcriptomic profiles of the hearts of HFpEF mice. HFpEF animals consisted in C57BL/6 mic that were fed a high-fat diet and exposed to L-NAME in the drinking water during five or eight weeks. Controls received a standard chow diet. Differential expression analysis yielded 1535 differentially expressed genes in HFpEF hearts relative to controls. 71 out of 78 DEGs contained in the GO-CC "Mitochondrial Inner Membrane (GO:0005743)" were found to be down-regulated, mostly affecting respiratory complexes I, III, IV and V in a time-dependent manner. Overrepresentation analyses also suggested that the mTOR signaling cascade is switched on, while "Diabetic Cardiomyopathy", "Cardiac Muscle Contraction" and "Cytoskeleton in Muscle Cells" KEGG pathways were detected to be affected, probably pointing at excitation-contraction coupling impairment. In summary, the transcriptomic program of the HFpEF hearts consisted in a widespread downregulation of the expression of the subunits of mitochondrial respiratory complexes, upregulation of mTOR signaling and deregulation of the genes related to the excitation-contraction coupling.

papers.title: Subchondral bone remodeling in knee osteoarthritis is coupled to lipid mobilization from bone marrow adipocytes
papers.abstract: Objective Pathological bone formation requires energy derived from metabolic substrates including glucose, amino acids, and fatty acids. As bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT) is a rich local source of fatty acids and is progressively depleted in osteoarthritic subchondral bone, we investigated whether lipolytic lipid mobilization is associated with osteogenic activity in sclerotic regions and whether this process is pharmacologically modifiable. Design Human knee osteoarthritis subchondral bone samples (n = 23) were analyzed using transcriptomic, histological, and ex vivo explant approaches. Associations between lipolytic and bone formation markers were assessed, with particular focus on PNPLA2, encoding adipose triglyceride lipase (ATGL), and alkaline phosphatase (ALP). Immunohistochemistry was used to localize lipolytic activation in relation to sclerotic bone regions. Ex vivo explants were used to assess adipocyte morphology, secretion of lipolysis products, including free fatty acids (FFA) and glycerol, and bone formation markers including ALP and P1NP. Pharmacological modulation of lipolysis was performed using forskolin to stimulate and metformin to inhibit lipid mobilization. Results Transcriptomic analysis revealed a strong association between ALPL expression and PNPLA2, suggesting a link between bone formation and lipolytic activity. Histological analysis confirmed local activation of ATGL in sclerotic subchondral bone regions. In explant cultures, reduced adipocyte size was accompanied by increased release of free fatty acids and glycerol, together with elevated ALP and P1NP levels. FFA secretion strongly correlated with ALP, supporting a relationship between BMAT lipid mobilization and osteogenic activity. PLIN1, a marker of lipid droplet integrity, was downregulated in isolated BMAT adipocytes but upregulated in paired stromal-vascular cells, suggesting transfer or utilization of BMAT-derived lipids by neighboring bone-forming cells. Pharmacological modulation confirmed that BMAT lipolysis is dynamically regulated: forskolin enhanced free fatty acid release, whereas metformin reduced it. However, short-term modulation did not significantly alter bone formation indices. Conclusion These findings identify BMAT lipolysis as a metabolic feature of subchondral bone sclerosis in knee OA. Mobilization of lipids from marrow adipocytes may provide energetic substrates that support osteoblast activity and pathological bone formation. BMAT lipolysis therefore represents a potentially modifiable metabolic pathway within the OA subchondral bone niche.
